items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: My father always put it this way because my father always used to listen to the famous band. I remember his famous band was like Wayne King and Guy Lombardo and this other fellow that played the trombone, Tommy Dawson.

ctx.x: Yeah. Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . And Claiborne, I would say, was like when I came to New Orleans, like Dave Poikin was. He taught both white and colored. Because I remember there was a white student and he had to go to their house and teach them, you see. And he was very known, I mean, as a very good teacher because there were many good musicians that came in colored and white that came to be a good musician that he had actually started. Now he was another one that used to go away with the shows and things. And he had a…
What about the funerals out there? Are they similar to the funerals here with brass bands?
